messages:
Aisha: Heads-up — ran an apples-to-apples priming comparison between replay harness (real traces, 95th perc seq 512) and a synthetic prefix-batched warmup. Goal: measure KV cache warmup, kernel selection stability, and autoscale interactions.

Tom: TL;DR numbers?

Aisha: TL;DR: replay warms KV cache faster (median tokens to 80% hit = 6.2k) vs synthetic (9.8k). Replay also caused more kernel churn and triggered fallback to fallback-int8 in ~15% of runs -> higher latency variance.

Ravi: Kernel churn how measured?

Aisha: Profiling: sampled traces + nvprof. We saw larger counts of small-kernel launches (attention softmax + reduce ops) during replay priming because token seqs had high variance. perf sample shows memcpy + kernel-launch overhead ~12% CPU overhead during priming window.

Marta: What about autoscale & burst credits?

bench-bot: run summary: {"run_id":"priming-2026-03-17","mode":"replay","scale_events":3,"scale_up_latency_ms":[3200,4100,2900],"burst_bank_used_pct":45}

Aisha: Replay triggered 3 scale-ups, avg 3.4s. Synthetic had 2 scale-ups, avg 2.1s, but synthetic consumed burst credits faster under steady high QPS because batching kept GPU busy and refill couldn't keep up.

Tom: So replay = faster KV hit but worse kernel stability + autoscale churn. Can we make kernel selection more stable during priming?

Ravi: Proposal: add a warmup-phase kernel-hint. If sequence variance > threshold, bias toward FP32/FP16 kernels that are less likely to oscillate to fallback-int8. Also cap per-worker kernel reloads during priming to once per 30s.

Marta: Any changes to batching heuristics?

Aisha: Tested "aggressive continuous batching" for synthetic: per-token CPU down ~8% but tail latency +5%. Config we tried:

``
warmup:
  mode: synthetic
  batch_window_ms: 12
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  kernel_hint:
    prefer_fp16_during_warmup: false
``

Ravi: For autoscaler, coldstart H2D dominates first 600ms. nvprof breakdown: ~0.6s H2D transfer + ~0.3s cuLaunch overhead. That's the big contributor to 99th latency during initial scale-ups.

Tom: Actionable items?

Aisha: 1) Implement kernel-hint toggle for priming (Ravi). 2) Add a priming-rate limiter to the synthetic harness to mimic replay variance (Tom). 3) Add scale-up backoff smoothing in autoscaler to prevent repeated scale events during priming (Marta). 4) Enhance perf telemetry: emit kernel-change events and a priming flag in bench traces (bench-bot will collect). I'll file GH issues.

Tom: +1. Also propose a lightweight "targeted-priming" that warms the most frequent KV keys (prefix sampling) to get faster hit rates without full replay noise.

Aisha: A prototype named "targeted-priming" is scheduled. I'll post results when ready.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline: priming-feature flagged -> rollout to canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC :rocket:

Marta: Thanks, this clarifies trade-offs. Prioritize kernel-hint and autoscale smoothing.
